title: File the annual unclaimed property holder report (California)
description: Businesses holding property that has gone unclaimed — uncashed payroll or vendor checks, customer credits and refunds, unused gift cards, deposits — must report and turn it over to the state each year, after sending the owner a due diligence notice before the deadline. The annual report and payment are due October 31 for general property. California splits the filing: a preliminary report is due October 31 and the final remittance between June 1 and June 15. Which state's law applies depends on the owner's last known address, or the business's state of incorporation when there is none, so a business can owe reports to several states.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee to file or register.

penalty.note: Interest of 12% a year from the original due date unless the failure was for reasonable cause (Code Civ. Proc. 1577).

title: Put freelance work of $250 or more in a written contract (California)
description: Under the Freelance Worker Protection Act (SB 988, from January 1, 2025), hiring a single-person freelancer for $250 or more, counting contracts in the previous 120 days, requires a written contract itemizing the services, their value and the rate and method of pay, with the parties' names and mailing addresses and the payment date. Give the freelancer a signed copy and keep it four years; pay by the contract date or within 30 days of completing the work. Retaliation is prohibited. Damages are in Business and Professions Code section 18100 and following.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee; this is a contracting requirement.

title: Classify contractors with the ABC test before treating workers as independent (California)
authority: California Labor Commissioner and Employment Development Department
description: California presumes a worker is an employee unless the business shows all three prongs of the ABC test: the worker is free from its control, does work outside its usual course of business, and is customarily engaged in an independent business (Labor Code section 2775, AB 5), with exemptions for some occupations. Misclassification means back wages, payroll taxes, unemployment and disability contributions and penalties.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee; this is a contracting requirement.

title: Notify residents and regulators of a data breach within 30 days (California)
description: If personal information of residents of the state is acquired without authorization, notify affected residents within 30 days of discovering the breach and the Attorney General if more than 500 residents are affected (Cal. Civ. Code 1798.82 as amended effective January 1, 2026). This is an event-driven duty, so it has no calendar date. Sources in the PR describe the state's rule in different words; check the statute for the exact trigger and content of the notice.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee to file or register.
